title: The Fisher (King Fisher)
tagline: Browser fishing-collection RPG: turn-based fish duels with seeded dice checks. Chapter 1 only (Village Canal and its King Fish).
summary: Chapter 1 of a browser fishing collection RPG that the repo's documents call King Fisher, built with React, PixiJS and Zustand. Fishing is a turn-based duel: the fish telegraphs an intent each turn and the player spends 2 action points on reel, pull, release, brace or observe, resolved by seeded d20 checks. Fish, gear, spots and story are typed catalogs checked by a validator; progress is saved locally in the browser. A GitHub Pages workflow deploys it.

claims.text: Fishing is a pure turn engine: applyTurnFishingAction(session, action, fish, stats) returns a new session plus ordered presentation events, ignores actions outside the player's turn or without AP, and takes every random number from an explicit seed (a 32-bit LCG). A Vitest test replays one seed and action list twice and expects equal results.

A check is a seeded d20 roll, with advantage or disadvantage meaning the higher or lower of two dice, plus a gear modifier against the fish intent's difficulty. The result is classed as critical failure, failure, partial success, success or critical success.

Fish behave by archetype: each archetype has its own weighted mix of five intents (steady pull, power dash, deep dive, thrash, recover). The King Fish uses the berserker archetype with phase changes at 60% and 25% stamina.

Content is typed catalogs checked by a validator that expects 1 area, 4 spots, 12 fish, 18 gear items and 6 story events, requires Thai and English text, and rejects a King Fish locked behind an event that cannot happen before the king-caught event. npm run content:validate runs it.
Saves use a strict, versioned Zod schema (version 1). decodeSave returns null for unreadable input, and the store refuses to overwrite an existing save that does not decode.

excerpts.title: Seeded d20 check with advantage and disadvantage
excerpts.why: The check is a function of (seed, mode, modifier, difficulty) and returns the next seed, so randomness is threaded explicitly and replays are exact. Bad modifier or difficulty values are coerced, and a natural 1 or 20 overrides the margin.

excerpts.title: One player action as a pure state transition
excerpts.why: A guard clause returns the same session if the phase, AP or fish id does not match. Otherwise the action builds a new session, the fish may answer once AP runs out, and presentation events come back beside the session instead of inside it.

excerpts.title: Validator: the King Fish must be reachable before the story says it was caught
excerpts.why: Content validation checks story order, not just ids: the King Fish's spot must unlock through an event earlier than the king-caught event, and its preferred bait must not unlock only after the catch.

limitations: Chapter 1 only by design: one area (Village Canal), four spots, one King Fish; PRODUCT.md says not to build later locations or multiplayer yet (E14).

No user research, player feedback or playtest record is in the repo; PRODUCT.md says to invent no proof points (E15). That section also still says no application or deployment exists, which is out of date.
The repo contains no screenshots or recordings of the running game; the images shown here are art files, not captures.
Test suites exist (engine, adapter, store, save, content validation) but were not run for this entry, so no pass result is claimed.
AGENTS.md names src/game/core/fishing/engine.ts as the state machine; that file does not exist at this commit (the engine is turn-engine.ts), so agent-facing docs have drifted (E16).
The Pages workflow also deploys two feature branches, so the live site may not match the pinned commit (E17).
Art provenance is mostly unrecorded: DESIGN.md calls the theme art newly generated without naming a tool, and the fish and canal paintings have no provenance notes.
The verification gate is documented, not evidenced: AGENTS.md requires npm run check (E18) but no run output is in the repo.
